title: A 30B model on a 4 GB laptop GPU

credit: The trick is llama.cpp's own option, --n-cpu-moe: it keeps the experts' weights in system RAM and the rest on the GPU. We measured it on this laptop; we did not invent it.
measured_at: 2026-10-25 (live take 11:13; llama-bench sweeps 11:20-12:10) - laptop on AC, Windows 11

benchmark, all experts in RAM (5 runs)

vulkan._doc: Second machine, same model: an AMD laptop iGPU over Vulkan (Ryzen node). 'expected' = the 2026-10-12 bench (docs/HANDOFF_2026-10-12.md 'VULKAN WIN on Ryzen'), a target only. The 10/25 re-measure writes measured_at / hardware (from lscpu + vulkaninfo on the box, not from notes) / command / results, then status 'take'. Only then does it render.

hardware.gpu: AMD Radeon 880M, integrated (RDNA 3.5, gfx1150; the Vulkan driver reports it as 'Radeon 890M Graphics') - 512 MiB of its own memory + an 11.3 GiB window into system RAM
hardware.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 9 365 (lscpu on the machine)
hardware.ram: 24 GB, shared with the GPU (22.6 GiB usable)

vulkan.gotcha: Every run first failed with 'radv/amdgpu: Not enough memory for command submission' - even with all experts on the CPU. llama.cpp pins the CPU-side weights as Vulkan host buffers, and on an integrated GPU that pinned ~12 GB overflows the GPU's shared-memory window.
vulkan.fix: --no-host 1 (keep the CPU-side weights in plain RAM) and -lm none. With those, the same 30B file runs on a laptop iGPU that has half a gigabyte of its own memory.

note: Speed swings with free RAM: Windows leaves ~11 GB for 12.8 GB of experts, so part of them streams from the SSD (16k-42k page-ins/s measured). See /methods/post03/.
units: GPU memory = nvidia-smi MiB / 1024 (GiB), the same unit as the 4 GB card
